title: Compact on-call cheatsheet generator and anchored diagnostics
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often need a terse, actionable summary of an incident plus a tiny set of telemetry "anchors" (small, replayable traces/log slices and metric snapshots) that let them triage fast without chasing large exports. This PR introduces a compact on-call cheatsheet generator and an anchored diagnostics collector integrated into incident-bot.

What it does: Generates a one-screen cheatsheet for an alert containing: incident summary (one-line), top-3 correlated signals, likely impacted services, recent deploys, suggested immediate mitigations, and up to three "anchors" — small, time-bounded telemetry bundles (tracelets, metric windows, and sanitized log excerpts) with stable anchor IDs. Anchors are small (<= 200KB each) and designed to be fetched or replayed by debuggers.

Design notes: Cheatsheet generation is deterministic: we run a ranking heuristic over tags and signal deltas, then format a markdown blob for chat posting and a compact JSON for the Console. Anchors are assembled from short queries against the telemetry store (traces and logs) and passed through the redaction filter pipeline before packaging. Anchors reference immutable anchor IDs so responders can request fresh fetches or cached copies. Anchors expire by default after 24 hours and are auto-pruned.

Security & privacy: All anchors pass the standard sanitizers (PII redaction, credential scrubber). Anchor storage is ephemeral and encrypted at rest (uses existing KMS key alias incident-bot/anchors). We added rate limits and size limits to prevent accidental data exfiltration. Customer-configurable policies allow turning off log anchors for privacy-sensitive deployments.

Implementation summary: Adds a new service command cheatsheet.generate (server-side), an incident-bot plugin that posts the cheatsheet to the incident channel and attaches anchor IDs, and a small CLI tool to fetch or replay an anchor locally for responders. The generator reuses existing ranking libs and the telemetry sampler but introduces a lightweight anchor packager and an anchor metadata registry.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests cover ranking, formatting and redaction. Integration tests exercise end-to-end generation with a sandboxed telemetry store. We validated size/latency: cheatsheet generation < 200ms on average; anchor assembly 350-500ms depending on trace depth. Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default off; enable for SRE on-call team in canary (2 weeks), then broader opt-in for oncall rotation.

Ops notes: Anchor pruning is a periodic job; added metrics for cheatsheet generation latency, anchor creation count, and redaction failures. Defaults are conservative (max 3 anchors, 200KB each, 24h TTL).

Related: Builds on ENG-1242 (cheatsheet ranking work) and SRE-998 (telemetry sampler improvements).

Files changed and diffs are intentionally small and focused on plumbing, UX text, and safety checks.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in compact on-call cheatsheet generator that posts a short summary and up to three ephemeral, redacted telemetry anchors (tracelets/log excerpts/metric windows) to incident channels. Feature is behind a feature flag and disabled by default. Admins can configure TTL, max anchors per-incident, and opt-out for logs.
rationale: Reduce time-to-first-action for oncall responders by providing high-signal, low-noise context and tiny replayable telemetry bundles without requiring large exports.
testing_notes: Unit + integration tests added. E2E run in staging against a snapshot telemetry store. Observed median generation latency <200ms; anchor assembly median ~420ms. CI matrix includes a mac job to catch OS-specific build issues.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged: 1) enable for SRE rotation (canary) for 2 weeks, 2) open opt-in to all oncall teams, 3) enable org-wide after 6 weeks if no major issues. Rollback: flip flag off to stop further anchor creation; pruning job will continue until anchors expire or pruning is disabled.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: primary risks are accidental data leakage (mitigated by mandatory redaction + size limits) and transient CPU/memory spikes during anchor packaging (mitigated with batching and memory caps).
notes: This is intended to be a conservative, ergonomics-first addition. The implementation is intentionally small to make reviews easy and to allow fast rollback if needed.
